title: Expires header is not a valid HTTP date
description: The Expires header carries a value that is not an HTTP date, such as `0` or `-1`. A user agent cannot parse it, so the attribute is ignored and the freshness decision falls back to heuristic caching from the other headers, which usually gives the response a longer life than the deployment intended.
remediation: Send an HTTP date, or drop Expires and express the lifetime with Cache-Control max-age. Never use the legacy `0` or `-1` sentinels.
limitation: One header value. The rule validates the date shape only; it does not compute the freshness lifetime a cache would derive.
